headline: Debora fell at home on 2026-10-02 and has since declined in function, now needing moderate help with bathing and lower-body dressing, while her spouse and caregiver Kevin reports exhaustion and asks for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-10-02 Debora fell in the kitchen while reaching for a cabinet. She had a small left forearm skin tear and denied head strike or loss of consciousness. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed. The PT evaluation on 2026-10-05 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see her twice weekly. A PT note dated 2026-10-04 calls the fall 'resolved' and removes it from the problem list, which conflicts with the 2026-10-05 findings.
items.verifier_note: The fall, the nursing findings, the PT evaluation details and the plan all match notes n005 and n006. The 10-04 'resolved' note (n018) is reported as a conflict for the team to resolve. The fall is not downgraded.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 OT found Debora needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing; she was independent at the last review. On 2026-10-19 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting her out of the tub, and Debora said she has been skipping showers because she fears slipping. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The OT note n002 and the home care aide note n001 match every detail in the statement.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, Debora's spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: Social work note n007 matches all details.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), and the pharmacist reconciled it on 2026-09-15. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks. No recheck is documented in the notes provided, and the later PCP notes (2026-09-26, 2026-10-20, 2026-10-27) say only that chronic conditions are stable.
items.verifier_note: Sertraline start date, PHQ-9 score, 4-week recheck plan and pharmacist reconciliation match the notes and the medication record. The three later PCP notes say only that chronic conditions are stable, with no recheck documented.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for this season, which began 2026-08-01. The last flu vaccine on record was 2026-04-25.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows no flu vaccine this season, a season start of 2026-08-01, and a last flu vaccine on 2026-04-25.

questions_for_team: The PT note of 2026-10-04 calls the fall resolved, but the PT evaluation of 2026-10-05 shows unsteady gait and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. Which is correct, and should the fall stay on the active problem list?
Have the walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars, tub transfer bench and handheld shower been provided? Should home care hours for bathing be increased?
What respite and evening support can be arranged for Kevin, and who will follow up with him?
Was the 4-week sertraline recheck, including a repeat PHQ-9, done? Is her fear of bathing or her mood part of the picture, and should the team review the fall in relation to the new medication?
Can a flu vaccine be offered this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) against the last IDT review date and note any gap in documentation before the window opens.
Falls and injuries: count falls, near-falls, and fall-related injuries in the window; check for fracture or head injury, and review gait/balance and assistive device use.
ED visits and hospital admissions/observation stays in the window: reason, discharge summary, and whether a post-discharge follow-up or medication reconciliation happened.

Cardiac status (ischemic heart disease, onset 2025, on metoprolol, clopidogrel, simvastatin, and PRN nitroglycerin): chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin use frequency, heart rate and blood pressure trends, bleeding or bruising on clopidogrel, and whether lipid or cardiology follow-up is due.

New sertraline (started 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms, PHQ-9 of 14): confirm the start date and indication, check for a repeat PHQ-9 after start, review sleep, appetite, and any GI upset, bleeding risk with clopidogrel, and whether a follow-up prescriber review is scheduled. Also check for suicidal ideation screening documentation.

Medication reconciliation across the window: note any starts, stops, or dose changes beyond sertraline, including the COPD inhaler regimen (fluticasone/salmeterol and albuterol nebulizer started 2026-04-25), and check inhaler technique and refill gaps.
COPD/chronic obstructive bronchitis: rescue inhaler or nebulizer use frequency, exacerbations or steroid/antibiotic courses, oxygen saturation if recorded, dyspnea scale, and smoking status.

Weight and BMI trend (obesity, prediabetes history): compare weights across the window for gain or loss, review any glucose or HbA1c results, and note nutrition or dietary concerns given possible mood change.
Thyroid (idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 0.075 mg): check whether a TSH result is due or overdue, and whether any recent results or dose changes are documented.
Breast cancer history and chronic sinusitis: check for any new oncology, surveillance imaging, or mammogram follow-up due, and any sinus symptoms or recurrent antibiotic courses in the window.
Chronic pain: pain scores, analgesic use (none is listed as active, so verify OTC or PRN use), functional impact, and whether pain is contributing to mood or sleep changes.

Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes since last review in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, meal prep, medication management, and transportation; cognition screen if one is due or if mood changes raise concern.

Caregiver and social situation: any change in living arrangements, caregiver availability or strain, transportation barriers, and social isolation, which may be relevant to the new depressive symptoms.
Attendance and engagement: PACE center attendance in the window, missed appointments or transport failures, and any care-plan goals or assessments that are due or overdue for update at this review.
